commit_message:
[json] Stringify: Move local fast-map-cache to DescriptorArray

Instead of having a local cache for fast iterable maps for each
stringify invocation, we store the information on the DescriptorArray.
That way it is shared between multiple stringify invocations and we
can also potentially use it in other places.

Drive-by changes:
- Remove ResumeJSObjectMode enum. We can directly use the
  FastIterableState from DescriptorArray.
- Rename FastJsonStringifierObjectKeyResult::kNeedsEscaping to kSlow, so
  we can also use it if we encounter a two-byte key (in a two-byte
  stringifier) to indicate that the map can't be fast iterated.
- Remove Map from ContinuationRecord. We previously only needed it for
  the cache.
- Rename ObjectResume_* Continuations.

findings.title: DescriptorArray marked kJsonFast after iterating only a subset of descriptors
findings.message: In `FastJsonStringifier::ResumeJSObject`, after completing the descriptor loop the code unconditionally promotes the DescriptorArray's fast-iterable state from `kUnknown` to `kJsonFast`. However, `nof_descriptors` is derived from `map->NumberOfOwnDescriptors()`, which may be less than `descriptors->number_of_descriptors()` because DescriptorArrays are shared among maps in the same map-tree (e.g. a parent map and a child map that adds more properties share the same DescriptorArray prefix). When only a prefix of the DescriptorArray has been validated, marking the entire array as `kJsonFast` is incorrect. On a subsequent `JSON.stringify` call for an object that shares the same DescriptorArray but has more own properties, `ResumeJSObject` is entered in `kJsonFast` mode and the code assumes `descriptor_idx == field_index` (the DCHECK at line 2774) without re-validating the never-iterated tail descriptors. That assumption is false, producing a DCHECK crash in debug builds and silent wrong-property reads in release builds.
findings.suggestion: Only update the DescriptorArray to `kJsonFast` if all descriptors in the array were actually iterated, i.e. guard the promotion with `if (nof_descriptors == descriptors->number_of_descriptors())`. This matches the fix in commit 7a68d07.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit (147949a0) moved the fast-iterable cache from a per-stringify-invocation local map to the DescriptorArray itself. The promotion logic at the end of `ResumeJSObject` does not account for the fact that `nof_descriptors` (the iteration bound, from `map->NumberOfOwnDescriptors()`) may be smaller than `descriptors->number_of_descriptors()` (the actual size of the shared DescriptorArray). The missing guard means a partial validation is mistakenly treated as a full validation.
